record.paper_title: Open Problems on Avoidable Patterns in Partial Words
record.original_question: How densely can infinitely many holes be inserted into an abelian n-free word so that the resulting partial word remains abelian n-free? Constantly bounded spacing between consecutive holes is ruled out by the cited result, so the question asks whether the gaps can be made smaller than exponential spacing, for example with distances between consecutive holes bounded by a polynomial.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A partial word over a finite alphabet $\Sigma$ is a sequence $w \in (\Sigma \cup \{\diamond\})^*$ or $w \in (\Sigma \cup \{\diamond\})^\omega$, where the symbol $\diamond$ denotes a "hole" (a do-not-care position). Two full words $u, v \in \Sigma^*$ of the same length are abelian equivalent if every letter of $\Sigma$ occurs the same number of times in $u$ as in $v$. A partial word $w$ is said to contain an abelian $n$-th power if there exist factors $w[i_0..i_1-1], w[i_1..i_2-1], \dots, w[i_{n-1}..i_n-1]$ of $w$, all of the same length, such that for some choice of full words $u_1, \dots, u_n \in \Sigma^*$ that are pairwise abelian equivalent, each factor is compatible with the corresponding $u_j$ (i.e., agrees with $u_j$ at every non-hole position). Otherwise $w$ is called abelian $n$-free.

It is known that there exist infinite abelian $n$-free partial words containing infinitely many holes, but that no such partial word can have the gaps between consecutive holes bounded by a constant.

Question: For each integer $n \ge 2$, determine the smallest possible asymptotic growth rate of the gaps between consecutive holes in an infinite abelian $n$-free partial word over some finite alphabet that contains infinitely many holes. In particular, can such a partial word be constructed in which the distance between consecutive holes is bounded above by a polynomial in their index (rather than only by an exponential function)?
artifact.status_search_result: The question of how densely holes can be inserted into an abelian $n$-free partial word, specifically whether polynomial spacing between consecutive holes is achievable, is listed as an open problem in the literature on avoidable patterns in partial words. Recent works on abelian pattern avoidance in partial words discuss constructions with infinitely many holes and exponential spacing, but no polynomial-spacing construction or matching lower bound appears to have been established.

status_evidence.title: Abelian pattern avoidance in partial words
status_evidence.snippet: Any pattern p with n > 3 distinct variables of length at least 2n is abelian avoidable by a partial word with infinitely many holes; the bound on the length of p is tight.
status_evidence.claim: Constructions of abelian-pattern-avoiding infinite partial words with infinitely many holes are studied, but optimal hole density is not pinned down.

status_evidence.title: Abelian Square-Free Partial Words
status_evidence.snippet: Bounds for the number of letters needed to construct infinite abelian square-free partial words with finitely or infinitely many holes.
status_evidence.claim: The question of optimal spacing of holes in abelian-free partial words is part of ongoing research with open subproblems.
